items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)
Experience with and/or ability to learn UC financial systems and reporting tools.
Experience in a college health or college recreational sports setting.
Minimum of 5 years management experience.
Proven experience in managing teams, budgets, and operations.
Minimum of 5 years of administrative experience.

The Administrative Manager oversees the following departments: Revenue generation / 3rd party billing, Budget - Health and Wellbeing, Finance - Health and Wellbeing, Patient accounts - UHS, the Business operations team - UHS, the Financial Analyst - Health and Wellbeing, and the Student Health Insurance Office (SHIO) - UHS.
Responsible for overseeing the UHS Business Services department which supports daily operations for UHS (Tang and satellite locations).

This position is responsible for overseeing and coordinating Business Operations, the Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP), and the Student Health Insurance Office (SHIO) within UHS. The Administrative Manager oversees third party billing, patient accounts, SHIP administration and revenue generation for UHS, while providing strategic financial leadership across three units to ensure compliance with UC, state, and federal requirements and supporting long-range planning, reserves strategy, and capital project financing.
Supervise the 2.0 FTE in the department.
Oversee the team who process purchasing requests, payable requests receiving, reimbursements, storeroom ordering (UHS) and aiding in travel planning.
Oversee centralized medical and office supply system.
Oversee price comparison and tracking of medical supply costs for appropriate patient billing.
Work with campus partners on vendor contracts and renewals.
Oversee procurement cards, reconciliation and reporting.
Ensure operational continuity and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency and cost control.
Third Party Billing and Revenue Generation
Develop a third party billing department.
Oversee accurate and timely billing to external entities, verify claims, resolve discrepancies, and maintain compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate with internal departments (clinical, finance, IT).
Develop strategies to minimize write-offs and bad debt.
Supervise billing, coding, and A/R staff. Track key performance indicators (KPIs) such as clean claim rate, denial rate, and collection rate.
Generate financial and operational reports.
Use data to identify trends and improve revenue cycle performance.
Optimize revenue cycle systems and electronic health record (EHR) integration.
Lead projects related to automation or system upgrades.
Collaborate with internal and external partners for claims processing and vendor contracts.
Manage vendor relationships.
Establish and oversee up-front credit and debit card payments.
Chair the Committee on Fee Impact and Eligibility and establish fee schedules and charge capture.
Ensure audit readiness and compliance with payer requirements, coding standards, and UC policies.
Student Health Insurance Plan
Responsible for overseeing the administration and management of the university’s student health insurance program (~11 FTE, ~23,000 enrollees).
Supervise the Student Health Insurance Manager.
Manage the plan's relationships with external UCOP/business partners.
Oversee UHS billing of SHIP and manage the plan's financial and operational performance.
Ensure that the insurance plan is compliant with state and federal regulations.
Direct overall management of the Student Health Insurance Office which provides member services and administrative processes for UC Berkeley students and dependents.
Manage relationships with external insurance vendors, ensuring that the plan meets students’ healthcare needs and that contracts are renewed or renegotiated in a timely manner.
Coordinate Request for Proposals for SHIP broker and SHIP carrier or providers.
Participate in the selection process for insurance providers, ensuring the plan’s offerings are competitive and meet the needs of students.
Oversee and track service level agreements (SLAs) with insurance providers.
Budget and Financial Management
Assist in the development and management of budgets for PTC, RecWell and UHS.
Supervise the financial analyst (1 FTE).
Monitor expenditures and ensure alignment with budgetary guidelines.
Monitor budget performance throughout the year, ensuring that financial resources are appropriately allocated and spent.
Provide regular reports and variance analysis to leadership on budget performance, highlighting any discrepancies and recommending corrective actions.
Maintain the integrity of the organization's budget reporting and tracking systems through supervision and oversight of budget and fiscal staff and protocols.
Develop, modify, and execute appropriate internal controls to protect University resources.
Work closely with campus for reserves and capital project financial planning.
Work with department heads and senior leadership to create, manage, and adjust budgets to meet organizational goals.
Collaborate with revenue cycle teams to ensure accurate and timely billing, collections, and reimbursement processes.

Lead training efforts to improve financial literacy and understanding across departments, ensuring all staff involved in budgeting processes are well-equipped to manage their financial responsibilities.
Provide guidance and oversee grant proposal and management.
Ability to approve timecards for all of UHS. Run staffing and salary reports.
Lead long‑range financial planning, scenario modeling, and multi‑year forecasting across all units.
Administrative Management
Provide operational, financial and policy guidance to UHS, RecWell and PTC.
Serve as a point of contact for managers and supervisors.
Suggest or oversee policy revisions.
Meet with internal and campus partners as a representative of UHS, RecWell or PTC.
Participate in professional development.
Encourage and oversee professional development of supervisees.
Participate in UHS, RecWell and PTC projects.
Serve as a key advisor to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Health & Wellbeing and H&W leadership and represent the division on campus‑wide committees.

Broad knowledge of and/or ability to learn the organization's processes, protocols, and procedures with a focus on budget, account, and fund management and / or personnel management under labor contract(s) and personnel policy.
Demonstrated understanding of revenue‑generation principles, including the ability to apply strategies and interpret financial drivers to improve overall financial performance.
Broad knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques; human resources and risk management planning; and/or accounting and payroll.
Strong verbal and written communication skills; ability to influence / persuade all levels of staff.
Skills in organization and customer service to effectively manage multiple important priorities.
Proven ability to organize department work functions in an efficient and effective manner.
Broad knowledge of common organization-specific and other computer application programs.
Skills to work collaboratively with other locations.
Proven skills to quickly evaluate complex issues and identify multiple options for resolution.
Demonstrated management and conflict resolution skills to effectively lead and motivate others.
